hook.text: Jung called his life's central idea individuation: becoming the person you were always meant to be.

buildup.text: It means integrating all parts—Persona, Shadow, Anima—into a unified self. It takes a lifetime.

discovery.text: Myths map this process. The hero descends, confronts monsters, and returns transformed.

twist.text: Individuation isn't perfection. It's accepting every part, including what you wish wasn't there.

climax.text: The Self archetype emerges: a mandala-like wholeness. Many myths end with the hero becoming king.

punchline.text: You don't find yourself. You assemble yourself.

quiz.question: What is individuation in Jungian psychology?
options: Integrating all parts of the psyche into a whole
